introduction.heading: Plumbing for Utah County homes
introduction.body:
Half of the homes in Utah County were built in 2001 or later, and about 25% before 1980, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. In newer homes like these, the first big plumbing jobs are often water heaters, fixtures and water softeners as the original equipment ages. A water heater usually lasts 10 to 15 years.

Each city in Utah County runs its own water system. Much of north Utah County's water is Provo River water from the Central Utah Water Conservancy District, treated at the Don A. Christiansen plant in Orem or pumped from deep district wells. Hardness averaged 133 mg/L (7.75 grains per gallon) in treated water from the district's Orem plant, according to the Central Utah Water Conservancy District's 2025 water quality report (wholesale water; each city's tap water can differ). The U.S. Geological Survey classes that as hard water. Hard water leaves mineral deposits in water heaters, faucets and appliances, and a water softener or filtration system cuts that buildup.

Central Utah Project water reaches north Utah County through the Alpine Aqueduct and the treatment plant in north Orem.
